rows: What algae gave rise to land plants?
Charophyte green algae — same pigments, cell division (phragmoplast), and biochemistry as land plants
What are the three bryophyte groups?
Mosses, liverworts, hornworts — non-vascular, gametophyte dominant, tied to moisture for fertilization
What is the earliest vascular plant?
Cooksonia (~425 Ma): tiny branching stems with terminal sporangia; first confirmed xylem
What made giant Carboniferous lycopsids possible?
Hot, humid, high-CO₂ swamp conditions; giant Lepidodendron (30–40 m) and Sigillaria reproduced by spores
Why did Carboniferous coal form?
Lignin-degrading fungi (white rot Basidiomycetes) hadn't evolved yet; wood accumulated without decomposing
What is the key innovation of the seed?
Enclosed megasporangium (ovule) — permits fertilization without water; embryo + stored food + protective coat
What is double fertilization?
Angiosperm-specific: one sperm → embryo (2n); second sperm → endosperm (3n); faster richer seed development
What caused the angiosperm radiation?
Multiple overlapping advantages: double fertilization, fruit dispersal, rapid generation time, pollinator coevolution
What is Darwin's "abominable mystery"?
Rapid angiosperm radiation in Early Cretaceous — seemed too fast for gradualistic evolution; now explained by synergistic innovations
What is C4 photosynthesis?
CO₂ pre-concentration in mesophyll cells before RuBisCO fixation; more efficient at high T and low CO₂; evolved independently 45+ times
